To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

long-term physical activity was associated with lower mortality from coronary artery disease, stroke, cancer and all-cause mortality in both sexes, and that the association was stronger for moderate and high physical activity than for low physical activity.
Long-term moderate or heavy physical activity in leisure-time is associated with a lower risk of dying from cardiovascular diseases, cancer and all causes in both sexes.

long-term moderate or high activity was in both men and women associated with significantly lower total and cause-specific mortality, and this association was independent of other risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of physical exercise in the treatment and prevention of cardiovascular disease.
the relationship between physical activity and health and disease.
the relationship between physical activity in leisure-time and subsequent mortality in a population of men and women aged between 20 and 93.

long-term moderate or high levels of physical activity in leisure-time is associated with lower mortality from coronary artery disease, cancer, and all-cause mortality.
long-term high physical activity in leisure is associated with lower mortality from all-cause, coronary heart disease, and cancer, but not for stroke and respiratory disease.
long-term moderate and high levels of physical activity in leisure are associated with significantly lower risk of death from coronary heart disease and cancer in both sexes.

physical activity is associated with a reduced risk of death from cardiovascular disease, cancer, and respiratory diseases in both men and women.
